title: 9 Ahrefs Alternatives for AI Visibility Tracking (2026)
summary: If you're looking for an Ahrefs alternative for better AI visibility tracking, we've compared 9 tools so you can pick the right one.
body_text: TL;DR Best overall alternative: Siftly Best for budget-conscious teams: RankScale Best for European and multilingual brands: Peec AI Best pure-play AI visibility monitor: Otterly.AI Best for full-stack SEO bundled with AI tracking: Semrush Ahrefs built its name on Site Explorer and one of the largest backlink databases in SEO, and for years that was reason enough to pay for it. In 2026, it folded a new module called Brand Radar into its core plans, promising to track how ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews mention your brand alongside your usual keyword and backlink data. On paper, that sounds like a convenient bundle. In practice, a growing number of teams are finding the AI side of Ahrefs doesn't hold up the way the rest of the platform does. Independent testing has caught Brand Radar undercounting AI mentions by a wide margin, the tool skips Claude and Grok entirely, and the deeper prompt tracking you actually need sits behind pricier tiers. If AI visibility is now a real part of your job, and not just a checkbox next to your keyword rankings, it's worth looking at what else is out there. Why You Might Be Looking For An Ahrefs Alternative Ahrefs remains a strong SEO suite, but its AI-visibility layer has drawn some consistent criticism. Brand Radar has an accuracy problem: Independent testing cited by multiple reviewers found it undercounting ChatGPT mentions by roughly 97%, in one case reporting 3 mentions where manual checks found 123. Historical data isn't stable: G2 reviewers report that past metrics change retroactively every time Ahrefs updates its index, which makes trend reporting hard to trust. No Claude or Grok coverage: Despite marketing Brand Radar as an AI tracking feature, it only checks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews. Prompt tracking is thin unless you pay up: The entry Lite plan only tracks 5 prompts, and getting to a usable volume means jumping to a $449 or $1,499 monthly plan. The core product has its own complaints: Ahrefs sits around a 2.0 out of 5 on Trustpilot across close to 300 reviews, with rising costs and credit-based limits coming up often. 9 Best Ahrefs Alternatives in 2026 Here's how the nine tools stack up before we get into the details of each one. 1. Siftly Siftly is built on a simple bet: knowing where you stand in AI answers is only half the job, so it doesn't stop at reporting. It's the only tool in this list that combines visibility tracking with the work of actually improving it, content and outreach included, and it ships as two focused products rather than one generic dashboard, Siftly Answers for B2B and service brands, Siftly Shopping for DTC and ecommerce. Ahrefs treats AI mentions as a side metric bolted onto a keyword tool. Siftly treats it as the whole point. Key Features: It checks up to 8 AI engines daily, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, so you're not relying on a weekly snapshot. It shows you which sources AI models actually cite, not just how often your brand gets mentioned. It auto-writes and publishes blog content with FAQ sections and schema markup built in, aimed at the specific gaps it finds. Its team runs citation outreach campaigns to help land the third-party mentions that AI models pull from. It connects to GA4 and Search Console, so you can see whether better AI visibility is turning into actual traffic and revenue. It ships as two products, Siftly Answers for B2B and service brands, and Siftly Shopping for DTC and ecommerce. Best For: Founders and marketing teams, from early-stage startups to growth-stage B2B SaaS, DTC brands, agencies, and regulated industries like legal and healthcare, who want tracking and the execution layer in one place. Pricing: Free — $0/month Starter — $79/month Growth — $249/month Scale — $599/month Enterprise — Custom 2. RankScale RankScale is for teams who care more about breadth than polish. It's the widest net in this list by a clear margin, and it runs on a single shared credit pool instead of rigid per-engine seats, so you're not stuck paying for coverage you don't use. It's also purely a monitoring layer, so you'll need to pair it with something that actually writes or publishes content. Where Ahrefs caps you at 4 engines and skips Claude entirely, RankScale flips that limitation into its whole reason for existing. Key Features: It tracks visibility, citations, and sentiment across 17+ AI engines from a single credit pool. It includes page audits, 50 on the entry plan and up to 200 on higher tiers. It connects natively to Google Looker Studio on every paid plan for custom reporting. Its "Prompt Decoding" methodology estimates real search prompt volume in your category, which is independently validated. Best For: Solopreneurs, agencies, and budget-conscious marketing teams who want the broadest engine coverage without enterprise pricing. Pricing: Pro — $99/month Growth — $385/month Enterprise — $780/month 3. Peec AI Peec AI comes out of Berlin, and it shows in the product. Most AI visibility tools treat everything outside English as an edge case. Peec built its default experience around it, which makes it the obvious pick if a meaningful chunk of your customers aren't searching in English to begin with. It's a leaner tool than most on this list, no content generation, no outreach, but what it does, it does with unusually clean, focused dashboards. Ahrefs barely acknowledges non-English markets exist. Peec AI was designed for them from day one. Key Features: It tracks visibility, ranking position, and sentiment across your choice of 3 out of 7 AI engines. It supports 14+ languages and multiple countries at no added cost on self-serve plans. Its Actions feature turns citation gaps into a ranked list of content and outreach opportunities. It auto-suggests starter prompts based on the topics your site already covers. Best For: European and multilingual growth and marketing teams who already know their priority prompts and want clean, focused dashboards. Pricing: Starter — $95/month Pro — $245/month Advanced — $495/month Enterprise — Custom 4. Otterly.AI Otterly.AI has been around long enough to earn some real credibility in this space, with more than 30,000 marketing professionals using it and a Gartner Cool Vendor nod in 2025. It's a specialist, not a generalist. There's no content generation, no outreach arm, just a sharp, dedicated focus on getting the monitoring itself right, down to a distinction most competitors gloss over: a brand getting mentioned isn't the same as a brand getting cited. Ahrefs bundles a watered-down version of this into a much bigger, unrelated platform. Otterly.AI built its entire company around doing just this one thing well. Key Features: It tracks brand mentions and citations separately across up to 7 AI engines, including Claude as a paid add-on. Its GEO Audit scores a page's AI readiness before publishing, with a predictive citation score attached. It runs AI Prompt Research to surface the real questions people are asking in your category. It offers a Google Looker Studio connector and API access on its Standard plan and above. Best For: SEO and content teams, in-house marketers, and agencies who want a dedicated, reasonably priced AI monitor without needing built-in content generation. Pricing: Lite — $29/month Standard — $189/month Premium — $489/month Enterprise — Custom 5. AthenaHQ AthenaHQ's pitch is that visibility data means nothing until you can tie it to something you already track, and it's built its pricing around proving that point. There's a real, no-catch free tier here, not a watered-down trial, and the paid tiers don't gate the attribution piece behind an Enterprise call the way most of this list does. It leans hardest toward ecommerce, with native Shopify and Webflow integrations most competitors don't bother with. Ahrefs gives you a mentions count and leaves you to guess what it's worth. AthenaHQ is one of the few tools here that tries to actually answer that question. Key Features: Its free Essential tier tracks 5 AI models including ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude at no cost. Its Starter plan tracks up to 9 models and includes a content optimization agent that keeps refining pages over time. It integrates with GA4, Search Console, Shopify, and Webflow to connect AI visibility to real traffic, included from Starter up. Its Ask Athena copilot lets you query your visibility data in plain language. Best For: Mid-market to enterprise brands, especially ecommerce teams on Shopify, who want broad engine coverage and real revenue attribution without a sales-gated entry tier. Pricing: Essential — Free Starter — $295/month Enterprise — Custom 6. Promptwatch Promptwatch sits in an interesting spot: it's essentially a cheaper, more self-serve take on the enterprise AI-visibility platforms, minus the sales calls and the six-figure contracts. It pairs its monitoring with an execution layer, so the gaps it finds don't just sit in a report somewhere, and its crawler-log analysis adds a layer most competitors skip, actual confirmation that AI bots are reaching the pages you're optimizing. Compared to Ahrefs, it gives up the backlink database entirely in exchange for going deeper on AI visibility specifically. Key Features: It tracks any 4 of 8 supported AI models with daily refresh on every plan. Its AEO Articles feature writes content tied directly to the gaps found in its Content Gap Analysis. It analyzes AI crawler logs to show which pages GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are actually visiting. It includes MCP and API access on every tier, including the free trial. Best For: Content and PR teams, and small to mid-sized marketing teams, who want monitoring and gap-driven content generation without an enterprise sales process. Pricing: Essential — $95/month Professional — $245/month Business — $579/month 7. Scrunch AI Scrunch AI plays in a different league from most of this list. It got acquired by Sitecore in 2026, and its whole design center is enterprise trust and control, the kind of compliance paperwork and crawler-level detail that only starts to matter once a company has legal and security teams sitting in on vendor decisions. Its sharpest feature catches AI models making things up about your brand, which nobody else on this list attempts. Ahrefs isn't even trying to solve this problem. If your organization has the resources to act on enterprise-grade data, Scrunch operates on a level Ahrefs was never built to reach. Key Features: It names the specific AI crawlers visiting your site, like GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot. It tracks 4 engines on its Core plan and up to 9 once you're on Enterprise. Its hallucination detection catches false claims AI models make about your brand, available on Enterprise. It connects to GA4 and Cloudflare to track AI bot crawl traffic alongside your visibility data. Best For: Large enterprises and well-resourced agencies that need SOC 2-grade compliance and have in-house teams to act on the findings. Pricing: Core — $250/month Agency Core — $500/month Enterprise — Custom Agency Enterprise — Custom 8. Semrush Semrush needs little introduction if you've shopped for SEO tools before, and in 2026 it stopped treating AI visibility as a bolt-on, folding it directly into its main "SEO & AI Search" plans instead of selling it as a separate toolkit. That's the appeal here: one subscription, one login, both jobs covered, if you're already living in Semrush day to day. The tradeoff is that full Claude and Grok coverage is still walled off behind Enterprise pricing. Ahrefs and Semrush have always competed head-on for the same SEO budget, so if you're weighing one against the other, the AI layer is now a real part of that decision, not an afterthought. Key Features: It generates AI visibility reports for any domain, plus sentiment monitoring and custom prompt tracking. It includes an AI-ready Site Audit alongside its standard technical SEO audit. It offers MCP access starting on the Starter tier. Its Enterprise plan adds full LLM coverage, brand and concept-level analysis, and ROI attribution. Best For: Marketing teams already invested in the Semrush ecosystem who want AI visibility bundled into their existing SEO subscription. Pricing: SEO only — $139/month Starter (SEO + AI Search) — $199/month Pro+ (SEO + AI Search) — $299/month Advanced (SEO + AI Search) — $549/month Enterprise — Custom 9. SE Ranking SE Ranking's whole identity is doing what the bigger names do for noticeably less money, and that holds true here too. It's fundamentally still a traditional SEO platform first, with AI visibility layered on as an add-on rather than baked into the core experience, so don't expect it to feel as native as tools built AI-first. If your frustration with Ahrefs has more to do with the invoice than the feature set, this is the closest thing to a like-for-like swap at a meaningfully lower price. Key Features: It offers rank tracking across 188 countries as part of its core SEO suite. Its AI Search add-on extends tracking across Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini. It includes an official MCP server exposing 160+ tools, including AI search visibility. Its Agency Pack adds white-label reporting and client seats, though only on annual billing. Best For: Budget-conscious agencies and small businesses that want one affordable subscription covering traditional SEO plus AI visibility as an add-on. Pricing: Core — $129/month Growth — $279/month Enterprise — Custom AI Search add-on — $89/month How to Make the Right Choice Choosing the right Ahrefs alternative comes down to what you actually need from an AI visibility tool, not just which one has the longest feature list. Here's what's worth weighing before you commit. Monitoring vs. execution: Some tools stop at telling you where you stand. Others, like Siftly, close the loop by generating content and running outreach based on what they find. Decide whether you want a dashboard or a tool that acts on the data. Engine coverage that matches your audience: Check which AI models a tool actually tracks, and whether they are included by default or locked behind a pricier plan, since several tools in this space quietly gate them. Citation accuracy: A mention count means little if it's undercounting by a wide margin. Look for tools that separate brand mentions from actual source citations, and be skeptical of any vendor that can't explain its methodology. Attribution to real traffic: AI visibility on its own doesn't pay the bills. Prioritize platforms that tie mentions and citations back to GA4 or Search Console data, so you can see whether the work is moving actual numbers. Pricing that scales the way your usage will: Credit-based and prompt-based pricing can climb fast. Map out what your prompt or credit volume will look like in six months, not just today, before picking a tier. Our Suggestion If you want a platform that goes beyond telling you where your brand shows up in AI answers and actually helps you show up more, Siftly is worth putting at the top of your list. It tracks up to 8 AI engines, shows you the sources those engines actually trust, and then writes and publishes the content needed to close the gaps it finds. Add citation outreach and direct GA4 and Search Console attribution, and you get a full loop from insight to measured impact, something Ahrefs' bolted-on Brand Radar was never built to do. You can start on Siftly's free plan and see your own visibility data before deciding whether to upgrade. Frequently Asked Questions What's the best Ahrefs alternative for AI visibility specifically? Siftly is the strongest fit if AI visibility is the actual job, not a side feature bolted onto a keyword tool. It tracks 8 AI engines, separates citations from plain mentions, and writes and publishes content to close the gaps it finds, something Ahrefs' Brand Radar doesn't attempt. Is Semrush a better choice than Ahrefs? They're close competitors on paper, with similarly sized backlink databases and similarly bundled AI tracking. Semrush's AI Search plans have their own complaints around pricing and prompt limits, so switching from Ahrefs to Semrush mainly solves an interface or ecosystem preference, not the underlying AI-visibility gaps. Can one tool fully replace Ahrefs, or will I need to combine a few? It depends on what you actually use Ahrefs for. Semrush and SE Ranking are built to replace the whole suite, backlinks and rank tracking included. Tools like Siftly, RankScale, Peec AI, and Otterly.AI are narrower by design and focused specifically on AI visibility, so if you rely on Ahrefs' backlink data too, you'll likely pair one of those with a separate SEO tool. Is there a genuinely free Ahrefs alternative? Siftly and AthenaHQ both have real free tiers rather than time-limited trials. Siftly's free plan includes AI visibility tracking across multiple engines, and AthenaHQ's free Essential tier tracks 5 AI models at no cost. Ahrefs alternatives AI visibility GEO AI search optimization

title: Wedding Cake Ideas and Guide: Flavors, Costs, and Trends
summary: The most popular wedding cake ideas for 2026 center on sculptural single-tier statement cakes, vintage Lambeth piping, and silver or pearl metallic
body_text: Last Updated on August 10, 2026 by Joy Editors The most popular wedding cake ideas for 2026 center on sculptural single-tier statement cakes, vintage Lambeth piping, and silver or pearl metallic finishes. Trending flavors include lemon-raspberry, tiramisu, and coffee-forward pairings. The average U.S. wedding cake costs $500 in 2026, with most couples spending $300 to $700 depending on tier count and design complexity. Buttercream designs run $3 to $5 per slice, while elaborate fondant cakes cost $8 to $15 per slice. Your wedding cake is more than dessert. It is the centerpiece guests photograph, the backdrop for your first shared slice, and often the detail that ties your entire reception aesthetic together. Whether you are envisioning a towering five-tier showpiece or a single sculptural statement, the choices you make around design, flavor, and budget will shape one of the most memorable moments of your celebration. This guide covers every decision point: the design trends defining 2026 weddings, the flavors couples are requesting most, a transparent cost breakdown by tier count and guest list, practical tips for choosing a baker, and a planning timeline so nothing falls through the cracks. Top 12 Wedding Cake Design Trends for 2026 Cake design in 2026 leans into two poles: ornate maximalism and clean sculptural simplicity. Both approaches reward craftsmanship, and both photograph beautifully. Here are the trends bakers and planners are seeing most often this year. 1. Single-Tier Statement Cakes With 18% of recent weddings hosting 50 or fewer guests, the single-tier cake has evolved from a budget move into a deliberate design choice. Bakers are treating these as miniature sculptures: hand-painted botanicals, sugar lace panels, and intricate piping that would get lost on a taller structure. A single tier also opens space for a private cake-cutting moment before the reception, with sheet cakes served to guests behind the scenes. 2. Vintage Lambeth Piping Lambeth piping (a technique originating in the 1930s that uses over-piped royal icing to create dimensional lace and scroll patterns) is the most photographed cake trend of the year. The look is unmistakable: raised borders, cascading swags, and intricate lattice work that gives a cake the feel of a vintage heirloom. It pairs especially well with classic ballroom and estate venues. 3. Silver and Pearl Metallics Gold has dominated wedding design for the better part of a decade. In 2026, silver and pearl tones are taking over. Think brushed silver leaf, pearlescent luster dust, and chrome-effect fondant. These cooler tones complement the year’s popular color palettes: dusty blue, sage green, and lavender. 4. Heavy Buttercream Texture Rather than smoothing buttercream to a mirror finish, bakers are leaning into bold, painterly strokes. Palette-knife textures, stucco effects, and swooping ridges give cakes an artisanal, handmade quality. The bonus: textured buttercream is more forgiving and often more affordable than smooth fondant. 5. Fresh and Candied Fruit Accents Sugared grapes, figs, blood oranges, and pomegranate seeds are replacing traditional sugar flowers on cakes this year. The look is organic, seasonal, and photogenic. Candied citrus slices add color without the expense of hand-crafted sugar work, and the fruit doubles as an edible garnish for guests. 6. Oval, Hexagonal, and Sculptural Shapes Round tiers are no longer the default. Oval cakes create an elegant elongated silhouette, hexagonal tiers add geometric interest, and asymmetrical stacked shapes bring a modern art sensibility. Expect to pay 10% to 20% more for non-standard shapes, since they require custom forms and more structural engineering from your baker. 7. Bold Monochrome Color Palettes All-black, deep burgundy, and saturated navy cakes are making a statement at evening receptions. The key is using food-safe gel colors and cocoa-based fondant rather than black food coloring, which can leave an unpleasant aftertaste. Monochrome cakes pair well with metallic accents: a matte black cake with gold leaf is a striking combination. 8. Floating Tiers and Vintage Columns Acrylic separators and vintage-style columns between tiers create the illusion of a floating cake. This architectural approach adds visual height without adding servings (and cost). Some couples fill the gaps with fresh flowers or small candle votives, creating a dramatic display piece. 9. Swan Motifs Swans are having a moment across wedding decor, and cakes are no exception. Sugar swans, swan-neck piping, and swan-shaped cake toppers appear on everything from single tiers to elaborate multi-tier structures. The motif connects to themes of partnership and grace, making it a natural fit for wedding celebrations. 10. Tiramisu-Style and Cocoa Finishes Inspired by the flavor trend (more on that below), tiramisu-style cakes feature exposed cocoa-dusted layers, mascarpone-textured frosting, and coffee-soaked sponge visible at cut edges. The deliberately “unfrosted” look feels relaxed and modern, ideal for garden parties, vineyards, and rustic venues. 11. Floral Meadows Around the Cake Base Rather than decorating the cake itself, some couples are creating entire floral installations around it. Fresh flower meadows, trailing greenery, and petal scatters transform the cake table into a focal point. This approach lets a simple, elegant cake shine while still creating a photogenic display. Coordinate with your florist and cake baker early so the floral design complements rather than overwhelms. 12. Baroque and Drapery Details Rococo-inspired sugar work, fondant drapery that mimics flowing fabric, and ornate bas-relief patterns give cakes an opulent, Old World feel. These designs require a skilled fondant artist and typically add $200 to $500 to total cake cost, but the result is genuinely breathtaking for formal, traditional celebrations. Most Popular Wedding Cake Flavors in 2026 Design gets the attention, but flavor is what guests remember. The best approach: pick a flavor you love, then choose two to three fillings that complement it. Here is what couples are requesting most this year, organized by category. Classic Favorites Vanilla bean with raspberry filling: The number-one request across bakeries. Light, crowd-pleasing, and pairs with virtually any frosting. Chocolate with salted caramel: Rich and indulgent, especially popular for fall and winter weddings. Red velvet with cream cheese: A Southern classic that has gone national. Best with a light, tangy cream cheese frosting rather than heavy buttercream. Lemon with elderflower: Bright and floral, ideal for spring and summer celebrations. The elderflower liqueur in the buttercream adds sophistication without overpowering the citrus. Trending Flavors Tiramisu and coffee-forward cakes: Search interest for tiramisu wedding cakes has risen 239% over five years. Espresso-soaked sponge with mascarpone cream and cocoa dusting is the most requested version. Champagne or prosecco-infused: The cake is lightly soaked in sparkling wine, giving it a subtle fizzy sweetness. Pairs beautifully with a champagne buttercream and fresh berries. Lavender and honey: Floral without being perfume-like when balanced correctly. Ask your baker to use culinary-grade lavender buds and local honey for the best result. Earl Grey and bergamot: A tea-infused cake with bergamot buttercream. Sophisticated, unexpected, and especially popular for afternoon receptions. Pistachio with white chocolate: The nutty, slightly savory pistachio paired with sweet white chocolate ganache creates a flavor profile that feels both modern and indulgent. Adventurous Pairings Matcha-yuzu: A Japanese-inspired combination gaining traction on social media. The earthy matcha sponge with bright yuzu curd offers a unique visual (natural green color) and flavor. Passionfruit-coconut: Tropical, tangy, and especially fitting for destination or summer weddings. The coconut buttercream keeps it from becoming too tart. Pandan with coconut cream: Another Southeast Asian flavor crossing over into mainstream wedding cakes. The natural green color and subtle vanilla-like sweetness make it a conversation starter. Flavor Pairing Guide Cake Base Best Filling Recommended Frosting Best Season Vanilla bean Raspberry preserves Swiss meringue buttercream Any Chocolate Salted caramel Dark chocolate ganache Fall / Winter Lemon Elderflower curd Vanilla buttercream Spring / Summer Tiramisu Mascarpone cream Cocoa dust (unfrosted) Any Pistachio White chocolate ganache Pistachio buttercream Spring / Summer Earl Grey Bergamot curd Honey buttercream Fall Pro tip: Most bakers will let you choose different flavors for each tier. A three-tier cake might have vanilla-raspberry on the bottom, chocolate-caramel in the middle, and lemon-elderflower on top, so every guest finds something they love. How Much Does a Wedding Cake Cost in 2026? Cake pricing depends on four main variables: tier count, serving count, frosting type, and design complexity. Here is a transparent breakdown based on current baker pricing across U.S. markets. Cost by Tier Count Tier Count Typical Servings Average Cost Price Range 1 tier 20-30 $120-$200 $80-$350 2 tiers 40-60 $300-$450 $200-$600 3 tiers 75-100 $500-$700 $350-$900 4 tiers 100-150 $700-$1,000 $600-$1,400 5+ tiers 150-250+ $1,200-$2,500+ $1,000-$5,000+ Cost per Slice by Frosting Type Frosting Type Cost per Slice Notes Buttercream (smooth) $3-$5 Most affordable option, delicious taste Buttercream (textured/decorative) $4-$7 Palette knife or piping techniques add labor Fondant (smooth) $5-$8 Cleaner lines, $1-$2 more per slice than buttercream Fondant with sugar flowers $8-$12 Hand-crafted sugar flowers are labor-intensive Elaborate custom design $10-$15+ Hand-painted, metallic, sculpted elements Six Ways to Save on Your Wedding Cake Display cake plus sheet cakes: Order a small, beautifully decorated display cake for photos and cutting, then serve sheet cakes from the kitchen. This saves 30% to 40% on total cake cost. Choose buttercream over fondant: The taste is often better, and you save $1 to $2 per slice. For 150 guests, that is $150 to $300 in savings. Use fresh flowers instead of sugar flowers: A single hand-crafted sugar peony can cost $25 to $50. Fresh flowers from your wedding florist achieve a similar look for a fraction of the price. Go with an odd number of tiers: A three-tier cake with a sheet cake backup often serves the same number as a four-tier at lower cost. Book early: Popular bakers fill up 9 to 12 months in advance. Last-minute bookings may include rush fees of 15% to 25%. Skip the delivery fee: If your venue is close, pick up the cake yourself. Delivery fees typically range from $50 to $200 depending on distance and cake complexity. When planning your cake budget, knowing your exact guest count matters. Using a free wedding website with built-in RSVP tracking helps you finalize headcount early, so you can order the right number of servings without overpaying. How to Choose the Right Cake for Your Wedding Guest Count to Cake Size Guide Guest Count Recommended Setup Estimated Cost Under 50 1-2 tier cake $120-$400 50-100 2-3 tier cake $350-$700 100-150 3-4 tier cake or display + sheet $500-$1,000 150-200 4 tier cake or display + sheet $700-$1,400 200+ 5+ tier or display + multiple sheets $1,000-$2,500+ As a general rule, budget about 1% to 2% of your total wedding spend for the cake. For a $35,000 wedding, that puts the cake at $350 to $700. Matching Your Cake to Your Wedding Theme Classic ballroom or estate: Lambeth piping, fondant, metallic accents, 4+ tiers Garden or outdoor: Buttercream texture, fresh flowers, fruit accents, 2-3 tiers Modern or minimalist: Clean fondant, geometric shapes, monochrome palette, 2-3 tiers Rustic or barn: Naked or semi-naked cake, fresh berries, greenery, 2-3 tiers Beach or destination: Tropical flavors, passionfruit-coconut, light buttercream, 1-2 tiers Vintage or retro: Lambeth piping, pastel fondant, swan motifs, 3-4 tiers Dietary Accommodations to Discuss with Your Baker More couples than ever are requesting cakes that accommodate dietary restrictions. Here is what to ask about during your tasting consultation: Gluten-free: Many bakers offer almond flour or rice flour alternatives. Quality has improved dramatically: a skilled baker can produce a gluten-free cake that is nearly indistinguishable from traditional. Vegan: Egg and dairy substitutes (flax eggs, oat milk buttercream, coconut cream) work well in chocolate and fruit-forward cakes. Vanilla vegan cake can be trickier; ask for a tasting sample before committing. Nut-free: Critical for large weddings where guest allergies may be unknown. Confirm that the bakery avoids cross-contamination, not just nut-free ingredients. Sugar-reduced: Some bakers offer naturally sweetened cakes using honey, maple, or monk fruit. These work best with fruit fillings and lighter frostings. Pro tip: If only a few guests have dietary restrictions, order a small separate cake in their required style rather than making the entire cake allergen-free. This gives everyone the best possible version of their dessert. Questions to Ask Your Wedding Cake Baker Walking into a cake tasting without a list of questions means walking out with unanswered concerns. Bring this checklist to every baker consultation: Before Booking How far in advance do you need to book, and is my date still available? What is your starting price per serving, and what does that include? Can I see photos of recent wedding cakes you have made in a similar style? Do you offer tastings, and is there a fee? (Most charge $25 to $75, often credited toward the final order.) What is your cancellation and refund policy? During the Tasting Can I mix flavors across tiers? Do you accommodate dietary restrictions (gluten-free, vegan, nut-free)? What frosting types do you recommend for my venue conditions (outdoor heat, humidity)? How do you handle structural support for multi-tier cakes? Logistics and Delivery Do you deliver, and what is the delivery fee for my venue? Will you set up the cake on-site, or does my venue coordinator handle that? What is your policy if the cake is damaged during delivery? Do you provide a cake stand and cutting set, or do I need to supply my own? When do you need the final guest count? Keep all your baker communications, tasting notes, and final design details organized in one place. A wedding planning hub helps you track vendor details alongside your guest list, budget, and timeline. Wedding Cake Alternatives and Dessert Trends Not every couple wants a traditional tiered cake, and that is perfectly fine. Here are the most popular alternatives couples are choosing in 2026: Dessert Tables A curated spread of mini desserts: macarons, cannoli, brownies, tartlets, and cake pops. Guests love the variety, and the display creates a visual statement. Budget roughly $8 to $15 per guest for a well-stocked dessert table, comparable to a mid-range cake. Many couples pair a small cutting cake (one tier, $120 to $200) with a dessert table for the best of both worlds. Cupcake and Donut Displays Cupcake towers offer the same tiered visual impact as a traditional cake with easier portion control and no cutting required. Gourmet donuts on a wall or tower display add a playful, casual vibe. Both run $3 to $5 per guest, making them a budget-friendly alternative. Interactive Dessert Stations Gelato carts, churro bars, crepe stations, and build-your-own sundae bars turn dessert into an experience. These typically cost $10 to $20 per guest but create memorable moments. A gelato cart is especially popular for outdoor summer weddings. Private Cake Cutting A growing 2026 trend: couples order a small, exquisite cake for a private cutting moment (just the two of them, maybe with the photographer) before the reception begins. Guests are then served a different dessert entirely. This lets you splurge on a stunning design without scaling it up for 200 servings. Wedding Cake Planning Timeline Cake planning fits into your broader wedding timeline. Here is when to tackle each step: 9 to 12 Months Before Start researching bakeries and styles. Save inspiration images. Book your baker. Popular bakeries fill up quickly, especially for peak season (May through October) weddings. Confirm your baker can deliver to your venue. 6 to 8 Months Before Schedule your cake tasting. Most bakers offer 4 to 6 flavor samples per session. Finalize your design concept: share inspiration photos, discuss color palette, and confirm tier count. Coordinate with your florist if using fresh flowers on the cake. 2 to 4 Months Before Finalize your design and sign the contract with a deposit (typically 50%). Confirm delivery logistics: time, venue access, setup location. Order any accessories you need: cake stand, cutting set, topper. 2 to 4 Weeks Before Submit your final guest count to the baker. This is when having accurate RSVP tracking pays off: you will know the exact number of servings needed. Confirm delivery window and point-of-contact at the venue. Pay the remaining balance. Day Of Have your venue coordinator or day-of planner meet the baker for setup. Keep the cake in a cool, shaded area (away from direct sunlight and heat sources). Save the top tier if you plan to freeze it for your first anniversary. Wrap it tightly in plastic wrap, then aluminum foil, and freeze within 2 hours of the reception. Staying on top of these milestones is easier when you manage your full wedding checklist in one spot. A planning timeline tool keeps your cake, vendor, and guest list tasks organized alongside every other wedding detail. Frequently Asked Questions What are the biggest wedding cake trends for 2026? The top trends for 2026 include single-tier statement cakes, vintage Lambeth piping with dimensional royal icing, silver and pearl metallic finishes (replacing gold), heavy buttercream texture with palette-knife strokes, fresh and candied fruit accents, and sculptural shapes like ovals and hexagons. Tiramisu-style cocoa finishes and baroque drapery details are also gaining popularity. How much does a wedding cake cost in 2026? The average U.S. wedding cake costs around $500, with most couples spending between $300 and $700. A single-tier cake starts at $120, a three-tier averages $500 to $700, and elaborate five-tier designs can reach $2,500 or more. Buttercream cakes run $3 to $5 per slice, while fondant with custom details costs $8 to $15 per slice. What are the most popular wedding cake flavors in 2026? Vanilla bean with raspberry filling remains the top request. Trending flavors include tiramisu (up 239% in search interest over five years), champagne-infused cake, lavender-honey, Earl Grey with bergamot, and pistachio with white chocolate. Adventurous options like matcha-yuzu and passionfruit-coconut are gaining traction for couples who want something unexpected. How many tiers do I need for my guest count? As a guide: 1 tier serves 20 to 30 guests, 2 tiers serve 40 to 60, 3 tiers serve 75 to 100, and 4 tiers serve 100 to 150. For larger weddings, consider a display cake plus sheet cakes served from the kitchen to save 30% to 40% on cost while still having a stunning visual centerpiece. What is the difference between buttercream and fondant? Buttercream is a whipped frosting made from butter and sugar that tastes rich and creamy. Fondant is a rolled sugar paste that covers the cake in a smooth, almost porcelain-like finish. Buttercream costs $1 to $2 less per slice, tastes better to most people, and handles humid conditions less well. Fondant gives cleaner lines, holds up better in heat, and provides a smoother canvas for hand-painted designs and sugar work. When should I order my wedding cake? Book your cake baker 9 to 12 months before your wedding, especially for peak season dates (May through October). Schedule your tasting 6 to 8 months out. Finalize the design and sign the contract 2 to 4 months before, and submit your final guest count 2 to 4 weeks before the wedding. Are single-tier wedding cakes in style for 2026? Yes. Single-tier cakes are one of the top trends for 2026, driven by smaller wedding sizes (18% of recent weddings had 50 or fewer guests) and the desire for highly detailed, sculptural designs. Bakers treat them as miniature works of art with hand-painted details, intricate piping, and premium finishes that would be impractical on a larger cake. What are good alternatives to a traditional wedding cake? Popular alternatives include dessert tables with assorted mini desserts ($8 to $15 per guest), cupcake or donut towers ($3 to $5 per guest), interactive stations like gelato carts or churro bars ($10 to $20 per guest), and private cake cutting with a small display cake plus a different dessert for guests. Many couples combine a one-tier cutting cake with an alternative dessert spread.

body_text: IMUNON to Hold Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Update Conference Call on Tuesday, August 11, 2026 August 4, 2026 PDF Version LAWRENCEVILLE, N.J., Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- IMUNON, Inc. (Nasdaq: IMNN), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing DNA-mediated immunotherapies, today announced that the Company will host a conference call at 11:00 a.m. EDT on Tuesday, August 11, 2026 to discuss financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 and provide an update on its clinical development program with IMNN-001, a DNA-based interleukin-12 (IL-12) immunotherapy, including progress in advancing Phase 3 clinical development of its lead candidate IMNN-001 in newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer. To participate in the call, please dial (800) 715-9871 (U.S. and Canada/Toll Free) or (646) 307-1963 (U.S./Toll) and ask for the IMUNON Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Call (Conference ID 8021948). A live webcast of the call will also be available here . An audio replay of the call will be available for 90 days and can be accessed at (800) 770-2030 (U.S. and Canada/Toll Free) or (609) 800-9909 (U.S./Toll) using replay access code 8021948#. About IMUNON IMUNON is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on advancing a portfolio of innovative treatments that harness the body’s natural mechanisms to generate safe, effective and durable responses across a broad array of human diseases, constituting a differentiating approach from conventional therapies. IMUNON is developing its non-viral DNA-based gene therapy technology across its modalities. The first modality, TheraPlas®, is developed for the gene-based delivery of cytokines and other therapeutic proteins in the treatment of solid tumors where an immunological approach is deemed promising. The Company’s lead clinical program, IMNN-001, is a DNA-based immunotherapy being developed for the localized treatment of advanced ovarian cancer. IMNN-001 has been evaluated in multiple clinical trials including one Phase 2 clinical trial (OVATION 2) and is currently being studied in the ongoing Phase 3 clinical trial (OVATION 3). IMNN-001 works by instructing the body to produce safe and durable levels of powerful cancer-fighting molecules, such as interleukin-12 and interferon gamma, at the tumor site. Additionally, the Company has completed dosing in a first-in-human study of its COVID-19 booster vaccine (IMNN-101). The Company will continue to leverage these modalities and to advance, either directly or through partnership, the technological frontier of plasmid DNA to better serve patients with difficult-to-treat conditions. body_text: See AuraStack AI Super Agent in Action! 18 Aug 2026 • 3 minute read Modern AI systems are pushing electronic design into a new phase of complexity. High-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, dense power delivery networks, and high-speed interconnects require engineers to optimize electrical, thermal, mechanical, and manufacturing constraints together rather than in isolation. The AuraStack AI Super Agent , built on Cadence Allegro AI Studio , extends Cadence's Intelligent System Design strategy into PCB and advanced packaging design. It connects design intent, implementation, multiphysics analysis, and optimization into a single continuous workflow. Connected Design Workflow The AuraStack AI Super Agent helps engineering teams keep power integrity, thermal behavior, placement, routing, and signal integrity analysis connected throughout the design cycle. This unified workflow enables earlier tradeoff decisions and reduces the late-stage redesign cycles that often occur when analysis and implementation are disconnected. System-in-Package Intelligence As designs scale into advanced packaging, coordination across electrical, thermal, and physical domains becomes increasingly important. Multi-die architectures, HBM integration, and dense interconnect structures require package planning, signal integrity, and power delivery to remain tightly connected. The AuraStack AI Super Agent extends its intelligence layer to support multi-die floorplanning and alignment, HBM integration and RDL planning, and high-speed interconnect and signal integrity optimization. This provides system-level visibility across PCB, package, and silicon, helping engineering teams improve convergence for AI accelerators, networking platforms, and other high-performance computing systems. NVIDIA Collaboration: Accelerated Engineering Ecosystem The AuraStack AI Super Agent operates within a broader Cadence + NVIDIA accelerated engineering ecosystem designed to support increasingly complex AI and high-performance computing systems. By combining Sigrity X Platform , Celsius Thermal Solver , Clarity 3D Solver , and NVIDIA Blackwell accelerated computing, the AuraStack AI Super Agent enables large-scale multiphysics simulation with faster iteration cycles, higher-fidelity analysis, and real-time design feedback. This integration helps engineering teams explore more design alternatives, validate system behavior earlier, and scale analysis across demanding AI and HPC workloads. Ready to Accelerate Your Next Electronic System Design? The AuraStack AI Super Agent helps engineering teams keep signal integrity, power integrity, thermal behavior, electromagnetic effects, and mechanical reliability connected throughout the PCB and advanced packaging design process. By bringing these domains together in a continuous, analysis-driven workflow, it enables earlier visibility into cross-domain interactions, supports faster design iteration, and helps reduce the costly late-stage surprises that often lead to respins. For AI accelerators, HBM-based systems, networking platforms, and other high-performance electronic systems, this integrated multiphysics approach provides a more practical path to achieving predictable system-level convergence from the start. Explore the AuraStack AI Super Agent and its AI-native approach to PCB and advanced packaging design, read the press release , and discover how Cadence is extending agentic AI across the complete electronic system design flow.

title: Archil: from a file system to a data company
summary: Archil (formerly Regatta Storage) has raised $6.7M to replace legacy cloud storage like EBS with infinite, shareable volumes that instantly connect to S3.
body_text: Archil (formerly Regatta Storage) has raised $6.7M to replace legacy cloud storage like EBS with infinite, shareable volumes that instantly connect to S3. The round was led by Felicis and Y Combinator, with participation from other investors. The Core Problem Cloud providers still require developers to specify storage capacity before launching instances—a paradigm unchanged since EC2's inception nearly two decades ago. This approach creates friction: guessing capacity needs, learning unfamiliar concepts like IOPS, paying for unused resources, and managing manual data transfers. Container orchestration systems like Kubernetes compound this challenge. "How do you deploy a 200 GiB model to a Kubernetes pod?" The tension between startup speed and data availability is real. The Archil Solution Rather than forcing users through complex configuration, Archil asks only three questions: volume name, cloud region, and data source location. The command to mount is straightforward: sudo archil mount $VOLUME_NAME This delivers a POSIX-compatible, multi-instance mountable filesystem with instant S3 bucket integration. We employ custom data protocols and NVME SSDs for performance—90% lower costs than EBS and 30x lower latencies than S3 directly. Beyond Storage: A Data Company Archil is fundamentally a data company, not merely storage infrastructure. Future capabilities include: Connectivity: Direct links to diverse data sources (Hugging Face, GitHub, data warehouses, SFTP servers) Compute: Serverless, low-level data transformations at the storage layer Intelligence: Built-in versioning, locality awareness, and access controls AI and Agentic Applications Recent developments show autonomous agents prefer cloud-agnostic, scalable-to-zero infrastructure. While databases dominated this space previously, agents increasingly require POSIX filesystems. Archil addresses this gap. We're excited to build the future of cloud storage. If you're interested in trying Archil, get in touch .
